description: Make terminal text bigger or smaller, and pick the font and weight (light, normal, medium or bold) it is drawn in, on this device only: a phone and a big screen can each keep their own. Every open terminal changes at once, with no reload. Prompt-theme icons (starship, powerlevel10k) draw through a bundled icon font whatever font you pick. Bigger text in one window can shrink a session you also have open in another window, because a shared pane takes the smallest window's size; the size crown decides which window sets it.
examples: On a 4K screen, press Ctrl+Cmd+= twice and every terminal is two points bigger.
On the phone, open Settings, terminal and set the size to 11 so more of Claude's output fits.
Pick JetBrains Mono from the list and the terminals switch to it; choose medium for a heavier stroke, or clear the box to go back to the system font.
how_to: Press Ctrl+Cmd+= for bigger text, Ctrl+Cmd+- for smaller, Ctrl+Cmd+0 for the default size.
Or open Settings, terminal, text: use a- and a+ (9 to 28), or reset.
Pick a font from the installed fonts list (each drawn in its own face) or type its name; it saves as you go and the status line says saved. Pick light, normal, medium or bold for the weight.
media_exempt: recaptured at the version bump with the other settings screens
name: Terminal text size, font and weight
summary: Change terminal text size, font and weight per device from Settings, terminal, or with Ctrl+Cmd+= / - / 0.
where: Ctrl+Cmd+= / Ctrl+Cmd+- / Ctrl+Cmd+0 from anywhere in the app.
